Therefore, using the watershed areas previously mentioned and assuming all other factors being equal, Tracts II and III would yield about 9 percent of the natural sediment generated within the Sarpy Creek watershed and Tract II would contribute only about 2 percent of that for the Tullock Creek basin.
On a conservative basis, it may be assumed that the potential sediment load could double from Tracts II and III as a result of mining activities. However, neither tract would ever be 100 percent disrupted at any time by mining and detention ponds will capture the sediment produced by most runoff even. Thus, the impact of sediment production downstream from the mine areas to Sarpy and Tullock Creeks should be minimal and may be less than under existing conditions. During periods of extreme runoff volume, precipitation exceeding a 10-year event, it is estimated that the sediment load contribution from the Project Area will be somewhat greater than what would occur naturally. However, the importance of such an increased sediment contribution in itself is not expected to cause a major impact because of the relatively small area involved in the mining operation compared to the overall drainage basin areas, and because during such a major precipitation event, receiving streams would be carrying high sediment loads due to natural erosion.
